The docs.wandb.ai/weave link now redirects to the CoreWeave-hosted Weave docs, and they cover your case directly. Since you aren’t using a supported agent SDK, you’re in the “custom agents” path. If your agent isn’t built with one of the supported SDKs, or it already emits OpenTelemetry spans, you use the Weave SDK directly. Autopatching won’t figure out your loop’s structure for you, so you add a few explicit spans.

Claude responded: The key is one llm.record(...

block, with Anthropic’s usage numbers adjusted to match what Weave expects. Weave shows token counts from the usage you record and computes cost from that usage plus the model id. If either is incomplete or unpriceable, you’ll see
even when the rest of the trace looks fine.
. The catch is that the two APIs define “input” differently. Anthropic’s
counts only the uncached part of the prompt, but Weave’s

must be the total input, including cached tokens. Weave prices cache reads and writes at their own rates and subtracts them from that total, so you pass the cache fields in addition to a total that already includes them.
Here’s an example of why the sum matters. Suppose Anthropic reports 120 uncached input tokens, 9,800 cache-read tokens, and 350 output tokens. You’d pass

. Weave then charges 9,800 tokens at the cache-read rate and the remaining 120 at the normal input rate. If you passed only 120 as the input, subtracting 9,800 cached tokens from it leaves nothing to price. The docs warn about exactly this: with prompt caching, cached tokens often dominate the input, so leaving them out makes usage and cost show up as roughly zero.
